source.title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). Characterize exactly when this Wijsman hyperspace is a normal topological space.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.
Problem 2.1 ([8]). Let (X, d) be a metric space. When is the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) a normal space?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). It is known that separability of (X, d) implies that (2^X, T_W(d)) is metrizable, hence paracompact and normal. Is the converse true: is the Wijsman hyperspace normal if and only if it is metrizable?

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

Problem 2.2 ([16]). It is known that if (X, d) is a separable metric space, then (2^X, T_W(d)) is metrizable and so paracompact and normal. Is the opposite true? Is (2^X, T_W(d)) normal if, and only if, (2^X, T_W(d)) is metrizable?

Problem 3.1. Is complete metrizability of (X, d) (without separability) equivalent to any completeness-type property of (2^X, T_W(d))?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A space is strongly alpha-favorable when player alpha has a winning tactic in the strong Choquet game, and strongly Choquet when alpha has a winning strategy in that game. If X is completely metrizable, then for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable?

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.
The space $X$ is \emph{strongly $\alpha$-favorable} \cite{telgarsky:87} (resp. \emph{strongly Choquet} \cite{kechris:94}), provided that $\alpha$ has a winning tactic (resp. strategy) in $Ch(X)$.
Question 3.9. Let X be a completely metrizable space. Must (2^X, T_W(d)) be strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable for every compatible metric d on X?

A space is strongly alpha-favorable when player alpha has a winning tactic in the strong Choquet game, and strongly Choquet when alpha has a winning strategy in that game. If X is metrizable and, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable, must X itself be completely metrizable?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A space is pseudocomplete when it is quasi-regular and has a sequence of open pi-bases such that every nested sequence V_n, with closure(V_{n+1}) contained in V_n from the n-th pi-base, has non-empty intersection. Base-compactness and subcompactness are Amsterdam-style completeness properties defined using open bases and non-empty intersections for centered families or regular filterbases. If (X, d) is pseudocomplete, subcompact, or base-compact, must its Wijsman hyperspace have the corresponding property?

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be (resp. \emph{countably}) \emph{base compact} with respect to an open base $\mathfrak B$ if $X$ is regular such that $\bigcap_{F \in \mathscr F} \overline{F} \ne \varnothing$ for each (resp. countable) centered family ${\mathscr F} \subseteq \mathfrak B$, and $X$ is said to be (resp. \emph{countably}) \emph{subcompact} with respect to an open base $\mathfrak B$ if $X$ is regular such that $\bigcap_{F\in\mathscr F} \overline{F}\ne\varnothing$ for each (resp. countable) regular filterbase ${\mathscr F}\subseteq\mathfrak B$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be \emph{pseudocomplete} \cite{aarts:74} if $X$ is quasi-regular and has a sequence $\{\mathfrak P_n : n \in \mathbb N\}$ of open $\pi$-bases such that $\bigcap_{n\in \mathbb N} V_n \ne \varnothing$, whenever $\overline{V_{n+1}} \subseteq V_n \in \mathfrak P_n$ for each $n\in \mathbb N$.
Question 3.11 ([7]). If (X, d) is pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact), must (2^X, T_W(d)) be pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact)?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A topological space is Baire when every countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense; it is hereditarily Baire when every non-empty closed subspace is Baire. Characterize, in terms of properties of the underlying metric space (X, d), exactly when the Wijsman hyperspace is a Baire space.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be \emph{Baire} if the intersection of every sequence of dense open subsets of $X$ is still dense. Note that a closed subspace of a Baire space may not be Baire. A space is called \emph{hereditarily Baire} if every non-empty closed subspace is Baire.
Problem 4.1. Let (X, d) be a metric space. Find characterizations for (2^X, T_W(d)) to be a Baire space, in terms of some properties of (X, d).

A topological space is Baire when every countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense; it is hereditarily Baire when every non-empty closed subspace is Baire. Let T_V denote the Vietoris topology on 2^X. If X is metrizable and, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space, must the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, T_V) also be a Baire space?

Secondly, it is known that the Vietoris topology on $2^X$ is given by $\mathscr T_V=\sup \left\{\mathscr T_{W(\varrho)}: \varrho \mbox{ is a metric on $X$ equivalent to $d$} \right\}$.
